beats: Two first-time buyers can put up to two hundred thousand dollars toward one home, without paying tax on the way out. Here's how it stacks.
First, the FHSA. Up to eight thousand a year, forty thousand in total. Deductible going in, tax-free coming out for a first home.
Second, the Home Buyers' Plan. Up to sixty thousand dollars from your RRSP, paid back over fifteen years.
That's a hundred thousand dollars per person. Two first-time buyers: up to two hundred thousand.
The twist: you can use both for the same home. And if your first plan withdrawal is between twenty twenty-six and twenty twenty-eight, repayments don't start until the fifth year after.
Add the home buyers' amount, up to ten thousand dollars on your return, and check every condition before you withdraw.
Next: couples, and who should claim the shared credits. Follow so you don't miss it.
